quarterly_data.signal: Full DESTINY-Lung04 Phase III results presented at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer: Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan, 5.4mg/kg) reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 37.0% versus pembrolizumab plus platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy as 1st-line treatment of HER2-mutant non-squamous NSCLC (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.50-0.79; p<0.0001), with median PFS of 14.3 months versus 8.3 months by blinded independent central review. ORR was 70.0% versus 44.5% and median duration of response 13.4 versus 9.7 months; median PFS2 was 22.7 versus 17.3 months (HR 0.80). Overall survival was 46.9% mature with no formal testing: median OS 29.3 months with Enhertu versus 33.1 months (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.88-1.52), which the company says may be limited in interpretation by imbalanced subsequent therapy (HER2-directed therapy in 48.0% of the comparator arm versus 23.3%). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events were 34.1% versus 33.6%, and adjudicated ILD or pneumonitis occurred in 20.8% of Enhertu patients, including four Grade 5 (1.8%) events. Susan Galbraith (EVP, Oncology Haematology R&D) called it the first Phase III trial to show superior PFS versus the global 1st-line standard of care in this setting (company claim).
